head_commit.message:
Stack the rounds below lg and reword the closed line

James's review of the Membership tab's build (#602, 2026-11-18): "The
rounds should sit in a single column on med screens. The closed line
should actually say 'Next pickup is Sunday, Nov 22', otherwise I
accept the build."

- A round's column is `col-12 col-lg-6`, so the rounds are one column
  below 992 px and side by side from there. They were side by side
  from 768 px.
- The closed round's line reads "Next pickup is Sunday, Nov 22". It
  read "Pickup is Sunday, Nov 22". The pill stays "Closed", which
  James accepted with the build.

His third point, that a pickup has happened at the end of its window,
is how roundsNow already behaves: the test lane's new tests for it
pass unchanged.

If this changes what a QA spec checks: the closed round's line and
the width at which the rounds sit side by side.

Make each page of the keyboard walk its own test

"every page tabs cleanly" walked the whole sitemap in one test, 10 to
12 minutes on the iphone project, and a lane could not run one page
(#607). When the site under test is the local build that
bin/e2e/serve.mjs wrote (e2e-run.yml builds and serves it before
Playwright starts), the spec now reads that build's sitemap as the
tests are collected and makes "<path> tabs cleanly" for each page,
plus /login/ and /404.html, at both widths. The walk, the settle and
the expectation are the old loop's body, unchanged.

builtSitemap only trusts a build whose addresses carry the origin of
E2E_BASE_URL. Against staging, or with no build on disk, the one test
stays and reads the sitemap at run time as before. A new test checks
the list read at collection against the served sitemap.

E2E_PAGES="/about/ /" narrows the per-page tests to the pages named,
and throws on a page the walk lacks, so a workflow input can pass it
without a free-form --grep.

head_commit.message:
Rebuild the Membership tab to James's design

Direction C of the #599 review, as James revised it (#602), replaces
the #597 layout he rejected for its hierarchy.

The group's name is in the account email's type with its address as
one small gray line, without the name again. Under it sit sections
at the page's section heading: Pickups, for a host Invite members and
Members, and for a member Membership QR code and Leave the group,
which now sit inside the member's own group and are h3s under its h2.
Every section heading has the page's gap above it, the member's two
included, which sat flush before.

A round is two lines, as James sketched it: the pickup's date in bold
("Sunday, Nov 22"), a middle dot and the window ("8:30 – 9:00 AM"),
each whole, so the line breaks only at the dot. Then, smaller and
gray, the pill at the line's start and when the round closes or
opens. Rounds are columns of a Bootstrap row (`row g-4`, each
`col-12 col-md-6`): side by side from 768 px, stacked on a phone. The
open round has an "Order now" button to the order page, where the
account's group brings its pickup and prices. A round between its
close and its pickup (#600) is listed first with a Closed pill.

Gone: the Rounds row and "every 2 weeks", the This round and Next
round subheadings, the label column and its subgrid styles.

The member's code does nothing at a market yet, so the tab shows its
QR code under a white veil and a "Coming soon" badge, with James's
paragraph. The code as text, the read-aloud line, the key tag and the
download are behind params.features.memberCode, which is off. The
server, the CLI and the key tag's page are unchanged.

Download QR code is now an outline button, so Order now is the one
filled button in the host's view.

Drafts for James: Closed, "Pickup is Sunday, Nov 22", Order now, and
the QR image's name, "Your membership QR code, not in use yet".

The specs change with the markup: membership.spec and
keep-together.spec read the rounds' two lines instead of the rows of
labels. qa: the selectors .account-membership-value, -term and
[data-mem-row] are gone.
